children: Bitcoin is on track for its longest run of weekly losses since 2022. As of the week ending November 15, the largest crypto asset had logged six consecutive red weekly closes.
The more interesting part is where the money is going. According to Bloomberg, longtime crypto investors are moving capital into AI stocks, prediction markets and stock perpetuals.
The slide has been steady rather than sudden. Bitcoin closed at around $86,480 on October 4, then fell nearly 24.5% to roughly $65,000.
It did not stop there. The price later broke below $60,000, a level it had not seen since early July.
Six straight losing weeks ties for the second-longest streak since 2014. The record holder is a nine-week decline in 2022, which makes the current run the longest since May of that year.
The exit is showing up clearly in exchange-traded fund flows. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $1.12 billion in outflows during the week ending November 20.
That marked the third consecutive week of redemptions topping $1 billion.
The wider market has shrunk along with Bitcoin. Total crypto market capitalization now sits at approximately $2 trillion, about half of its peak levels from 2024 and 2025.

Bloomberg's reporting points to three destinations for the departing capital. The first is AI stocks, which have dominated the speculative conversation in equities. The second is prediction markets. These platforms let users wager on the outcome of real-world events, from elections to economic data. The third is stock perpetuals. A perpetual is a derivatives contract with no expiry date, a structure crypto traders know well from Bitcoin futures, now pointed at equities instead.

Bitcoin's drop below $60,000 came amid a broader pullback in risk appetite, driven in part by a selloff in tech stocks, especially the AI sector. That selloff has been tied to concerns about whether the current pace of AI infrastructure spending can be sustained.

The ETF data adds a second layer. Spot products were supposed to anchor steadier, longer-term demand, yet three consecutive weeks of $1 billion-plus outflows show those vehicles can amplify selling just as easily as buying.

Several markers are worth tracking from here. The first is whether the weekly streak extends toward the nine-week benchmark set in 2022, or whether a green close finally breaks it. The second is ETF flows. A slowdown in redemptions would suggest the rotation is losing steam, while a fourth straight billion-dollar week would point the other way. Finally, the $60,000 level now carries extra weight. Having broken below it for the first time since early July, Bitcoin's ability to reclaim it, or failure to do so, will shape how traders read the next leg of this market.

title: Bitcoin heads for longest weekly losing streak since 2022 as holders chase AI stocks
